newsitem.title: USA: Rubin sees continued solid growth, low inflation.
newsitem.headline: Rubin sees continued solid growth, low inflation.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Monday that he sees solid U.S. economic growth with low inflation for the foreseeable future.
"The most likely scenario going forward as far as I care to look into the future is for continued solid growth and low inflation," he told the House Judiciary Committee.

But eventually, he added, the United States will suffer another economic slowdown. That is why the U.S. government needs the flexibility to respond and why the proposed balanced budget amendment to the Constitution is a bad idea, he said.

Rubin acknowledged that many state governments in the United States are required to balance their budgets. But they have separate "capital" budgets that cover investment and are exempt from the requirement that they be balanced, Rubin said.
He said that he personally opposes the adoption of a capital budget by the federal government.
But he said that one might be adopted "in the not too distant future," although passage of a balanced budget amendment would preclude that from happening.
Rubin also argued that the federal government has a much bigger impact on the U.S. economy than the states and that is another reason why a balanced budget amendment is a bad idea.
